name: Fabric Folds
basis: sine-wave folds bent by brightness, lit as cloth (how)
note: Drapery is an arrangement of cloth, not a making process; the woven grain is texture only.

lumenary.blurb: Cloth hung in soft folds, the folds bent into the shape of your picture. Printed or plain, with a woven grain.

facts.from: Studies of drapery in painting and sculpture
facts.bestOn: Pictures with smooth shapes and wide tonal range

why: Hanging cloth falls in folds that run in one direction, and each fold is a wave across the cloth. By adding the picture’s brightness inside the wave, the folds bend wherever the picture changes, so the cloth seems to drape over the scene. Soft shading and a woven grain do the rest.
how: Compute each fold as a sine of the position measured along the hang direction.
Add the picture’s brightness inside the sine so folds bend over its shapes, with slow noise to make them wander.
Add a second sine at 2.3 times the frequency and a bump proportional to brightness for secondary ripples.
Light the slope of the height map with diffuse light, a broad highlight and a soft rim of light at grazing angles where fibres scatter light.
Dim the shading slightly with a woven grain made from two cosines, and print the picture on the cloth or use one chosen colour.
history: Artists have studied drapery for centuries. Leonardo da Vinci made careful studies of cloth dipped in clay and draped over models, and Renaissance workshops treated folded fabric as a test of skill in both painting and marble. The rim light used for the fibres is a standard trick for velvet and satin in computer graphics.
terms: Cloth shown hanging or falling in folds.
A soft glow at the edge of a surface seen at a grazing angle.
The lengthwise and crosswise threads of a woven cloth.
paragraphs: Cloth hung from above falls in folds that run in one direction. Each fold is a wave across the cloth: a sine of position, measured along the hang direction. To make the cloth drape over your picture, the picture’s brightness is added inside the sine, so the folds bend wherever the picture changes; a slow noise also nudges the position, so the folds wander. A second sine at 2.3 times the frequency, and a bump proportional to brightness, give the folds secondary ripples and make the shape of the picture stand out.

The slope of this height map is the surface normal. Cloth is lit with a diffuse term plus a broad specular highlight, and one more thing that distinguishes it from stone: a soft rim of light at grazing angles, where fibres standing up scatter light, proportional to (1 − n_z)². A woven grain, a product of two cosines at a thread spacing of a couple of pixels, dims the shading slightly. The cloth is either the picture’s own colours (softened) printed on the fabric, or one chosen colour.

equations.note: Phase of the folds: f is the number of folds, w = 1.6 × the “picture bends the folds” slider, θ the hang direction and η the slow wander.
Final colour: g is the weave factor (about 0.93 to 1), σ the sheen slider, m the half vector; the last term is the rim light of standing fibres.

presets.text: Gold cloth with a strong sheen looks like satin.
Many fine folds read like pleated silk.
Let the picture bend the folds as much as possible.
